title: Naturality of endomorphisms propagated along span completions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category], let $W$ be a wide subcategory (it contains every object and identity and is closed under composition) satisfying two-out-of-three: if two of $f,g,gf$ lie in $W$, so does the third. Let $U\subseteq W$ be a wide subcategory. Fix a functorial square-completion rule $S$: for each span $D\xleftarrow{q}B\xrightarrow{h}B'$ with $q\in U$, it chooses $D\xrightarrow{k}D'\xleftarrow{q'}B'$ with $q'\in U$ and $kq=q'h$. On every commuting triple of maps of input spans it chooses a map of output vertices commuting with $k,q'$, and these choices preserve identities and composition. Fix $n\geq0$, a chain $B_0\xrightarrow{h_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_n}B_n$, and $q_0:B_0\to D_0$ in $U$. Recursively let $(D_j,k_j:D_{j-1}\to D_j,q_j:B_j\to D_j)$ be the output of $S$ on $(D_{j-1}\xleftarrow{q_{j-1}}B_{j-1}\xrightarrow{h_j}B_j)$ for $1\leq j\leq n$. Choose $e_0:D_0\to D_0$ fixing $q_0$, i.e. $e_0q_0=q_0$, and let $e_j$, $1\leq j\leq n$, be the specified endomorphisms of [lem-coef-iterated-span-fixed-endomorphism]: $e_j$ is the output-vertex map of $S$ on the input-span endomorphism $(e_{j-1},1_{B_{j-1}},1_{B_j})$. Take a second chain $\widetilde B_0\xrightarrow{\widetilde h_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{\widetilde h_n}\widetilde B_n$, an arrow $\widetilde q_0:\widetilde B_0\to\widetilde D_0$ in $U$, and an endomorphism $\widetilde e_0$ with $\widetilde e_0\widetilde q_0=\widetilde q_0$; let $\widetilde D_j,\widetilde k_j,\widetilde q_j,\widetilde e_j$ be obtained by the same rule $S$. Suppose maps $a_j:B_j\to\widetilde B_j$ and $t_0:D_0\to\widetilde D_0$ satisfy
$$a_jh_j=\widetilde h_ja_{j-1},\qquad t_0q_0=\widetilde q_0a_0,\qquad t_0e_0=\widetilde e_0t_0.$$
Let $t_j:D_j\to\widetilde D_j$ be the output-vertex map of $S$ on the input-span map $(t_{j-1},a_{j-1},a_j)$. Then these input-span maps are well-defined and
$$t_jq_j=\widetilde q_ja_j,\qquad t_jk_j=\widetilde k_jt_{j-1},\qquad t_je_j=\widetilde e_jt_j\quad(1\leq j\leq n).$$
Thus the specified endomorphisms commute with every map of initial chains and anchors intertwining the initial endomorphisms; in particular they form natural endomorphisms for any category of such input data.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 8.2(i), printed p. 29 (PDF p. 13), following Proofs paragraph; explicit auxiliary assertion extracted from the square-criterion proof step 5. No Stacks tag is claimed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-iterated-span-fixed-endomorphism] separately to the two chains with their given anchors and initial endomorphisms. Its hypotheses are exactly the common category, wide subcategories $U\subseteq W$, two-out-of-three for $W$, the given completion rule $S$, and the two initial fixed-anchor equations. Thus all the specified span endomorphisms exist, and $e_iq_i=q_i$ and $\widetilde e_i\widetilde q_i=\widetilde q_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$ (at $i=0$ these are hypotheses). We use the specified output maps in that statement, not an arbitrary choice of endomorphisms satisfying its equations.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: historical auxiliary chain-completion naturality argument, explicitly supplied by the worker; see inherited blueprint.from.place and square-criterion proof step 8.

proof.text: Induct on $j$ to construct $t_i$ for $0\leq i\leq j$ and prove the anchor equation $t_iq_i=\widetilde q_i a_i$ and the intertwining equation $t_ie_i=\widetilde e_i t_i$ at every such $i$, as well as $t_ik_i=\widetilde k_i t_{i-1}$ for $1\leq i\leq j$. For $j=0$ the first two equations are the hypotheses on $t_0$ and there is no transition equation to check. In particular this already proves the assertion when $n=0$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: historical auxiliary chain-completion naturality argument, explicitly supplied by the worker; see inherited blueprint.from.place and square-criterion proof step 8.

proof.text: For $1\leq j\leq n$, assume the assertion through $j-1$. The two equations needed for $T_j=(t_{j-1},a_{j-1},a_j)$ to be a map of input spans are $t_{j-1}q_{j-1}=\widetilde q_{j-1}a_{j-1}$, supplied by induction, and $a_jh_j=\widetilde h_ja_{j-1}$, supplied by the chain-map hypothesis. Both input legs belong to $U$ by the recursive construction. Hence $S$ is defined on $T_j$. Write $S_*(T_j)=t_j$ for its output-vertex map. By the assumed commutation of that output map with the two output legs, $t_jq_j=\widetilde q_ja_j$ and $t_jk_j=\widetilde k_jt_{j-1}$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: historical auxiliary chain-completion naturality argument, explicitly supplied by the worker; see inherited blueprint.from.place and square-criterion proof step 8.

proof.text: Let $E_j=(e_{j-1},1_{B_{j-1}},1_{B_j})$ and $\widetilde E_j=(\widetilde e_{j-1},1_{\widetilde B_{j-1}},1_{\widetilde B_j})$ be the input-span endomorphisms established in step 1. Composition of span maps is componentwise. Thus $T_jE_j=(t_{j-1}e_{j-1},a_{j-1},a_j)$ and $\widetilde E_jT_j=(\widetilde e_{j-1}t_{j-1},a_{j-1},a_j)$. The induction hypothesis on the first components gives $T_jE_j=\widetilde E_jT_j$. Apply the output-vertex assignment $S_*$ and use its assumed preservation of composition: $$t_je_j=S_*(T_j)S_*(E_j)=S_*(T_jE_j)=S_*(\widetilde E_jT_j)=S_*(\widetilde E_j)S_*(T_j)=\widetilde e_jt_j.$$ Here $S_*(E_j)=e_j$ and $S_*(\widetilde E_j)=\widetilde e_j$ by their specified definitions. This completes the induction.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: historical auxiliary chain-completion naturality argument, explicitly supplied by the worker; see inherited blueprint.from.place and square-criterion proof step 8.

proof.text: For completeness, on any category of the stated input data, the assignments of output vertices are functorial: an identity input map gives $t_0=1$ and all $a_i=1$, so induction and preservation of identities by $S_*$ give $t_j=1$. For composable input maps with chain components $a_i,b_i$ and recursively induced vertex maps $t_i,u_i$, induction gives the preceding vertex component $u_{j-1}t_{j-1}$ for their composite. Its span map is therefore the composite of the two span maps, and preservation of composition gives output map $u_jt_j$. Consequently evaluation at each output vertex is a functor, and the equations $t_je_j=\widetilde e_jt_j$ just proved are exactly the naturality equations for its specified endomorphisms. The equations involving $q_j,k_j$ give the asserted compatibility along the completed chains.

lean.statement: theorem iteratedSpanEndomorphismNaturality (W U : MorphismProperty C) [W.IsMultiplicative] [W.HasTwoOutOfThreeProperty] [U.IsMultiplicative] (hUW : U ≤ W) (rule : IteratedSpanCompletionRule U) (B B' : ℕ → C) (h : ∀ j : ℕ, B j ⟶ B (j + 1)) (h' : ∀ j : ℕ, B' j ⟶ B' (j + 1)) (s₀ : IteratedSpanState rule B h 0) (s₀' : IteratedSpanState rule B' h' 0) (x₀ : IteratedSpanFixedState rule s₀) (x₀' : IteratedSpanFixedState rule s₀') (a : ∀ j : ℕ, B j ⟶ B' j) (ha : ∀ j : ℕ, h j ≫ a (j + 1) = a j ≫ h' j) (t₀ : s₀.D ⟶ s₀'.D) (ht₀ : s₀.q ≫ t₀ = a 0 ≫ s₀'.q) (ht₀e : t₀ ≫ x₀'.e = x₀.e ≫ t₀) (n : ℕ) : (∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ n → (iteratedSpanStateAt s₀ j).q ≫ (iteratedSpanMapStateAt s₀ s₀' a ha t₀ ht₀ j).t = a j ≫ (iteratedSpanStateAt s₀' j).q) ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, j < n → (IteratedSpanState.transition (iteratedSpanStateAt s₀ j)) ≫ (iteratedSpanMapStateAt s₀ s₀' a ha t₀ ht₀ (j + 1)).t = (iteratedSpanMapStateAt s₀ s₀' a ha t₀ ht₀ j).t ≫ (IteratedSpanState.transition (iteratedSpanStateAt s₀' j))) ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ n → (iteratedSpanMapStateAt s₀ s₀' a ha t₀ ht₀ j).t ≫ (iteratedSpanFixedStateAt x₀' j).e = (iteratedSpanFixedStateAt x₀ j).e ≫ (iteratedSpanMapStateAt s₀ s₀' a ha t₀ ht₀ j).t)
